goal: Show the developer how to intercept WebView2 new-window requests and either suppress them or redirect them to an in-app WebView2.
must_include: Hooks `CoreWebView2.NewWindowRequested` after the control has been initialized with `EnsureCoreWebView2Async`.
For opening in the same embedded browser, assigns `e.NewWindow` to an existing `CoreWebView2` instance or navigates the current control explicitly and marks the request handled as appropriate.
Keeps the solution in WebView2 event handling rather than trying to manage external Edge windows after they appear.
must_not: Uses `Process.Kill` or window-title automation to close new browser windows.
Adds JavaScript that removes every link target without handling `window.open()` and other new-window requests.
Subscribes to `NewWindowRequested` before `CoreWebView2` exists without awaiting initialization.
Tells them WebView2 cannot intercept new-window requests.
acceptable_alternatives: Create a second in-app WebView2 tab/window and set `e.NewWindow` to that instance.
Cancel all new-window requests with `e.Handled = true` when the product requirement is no popups.
Use navigation filtering in addition to `NewWindowRequested` for domain allow-listing.
solved: The answer provides a WinForms-compatible `NewWindowRequested` handler that is registered after initialization and either cancels or redirects target-blank/window.open requests inside the app.
partial: The answer names `NewWindowRequested` but does not show when to hook it or how to block/redirect the event.
notes: The accepted answer sets `e.NewWindow` to the existing `CoreWebView2`; blocking with `Handled=true` is also correct when that is the stated behavior.
